`return` inside the clause that runs on the way out it replaces whatever the block was leaving with, so a failure raised in the body disappears and nothing records that it happened Fix: move it after the block, so the block's own exit is preserved
Calls itself 1 times per invocation with no memo in sight. nothing can stop the recursion, so the first call exhausts the stack Fix: give `loops` the case that answers without calling itself

`rows` is changed while it is being walked. the iteration and the mutation disagree about what remains, so elements are skipped or visited twice depending on where the change lands Fix: collect what to change, and change it after the walk
`case 1:` runs on into the arm below the arm below also runs, and nothing here says whether that was intended Fix: end the arm, or say in the code that falling through is the point
`(kind === "a")` is asked twice in one chain the second branch cannot be reached, so whatever it was written to do has never run Fix: decide which of the two arms was meant, and delete the other

Both arms of this branch do the same thing. the decision changes nothing, so either it is not a decision or one branch was meant to differ Fix: keep one body and delete the branch, or make the arms differ

`count` is compared against itself. the result is decided before the comparison runs, so either it does nothing or one side was meant to be a different expression Fix: one side was meant to be something else; decide which

`found = a + b` assigns where a condition is expected. it reads as a comparison and behaves as an assignment, so an accidental assignment is easy to miss in review Fix: assign above the branch, or compare if that is what was meant

This catch clause has an empty body. the failure is swallowed silently, so it first appears as wrong data elsewhere, with nothing in the logs to connect the two Fix: log it, rethrow it, or write the reason ignoring it is correct

This statement cannot run: the block always returns before reaching it. this code cannot run, so whatever it was written to do is not happening Fix: delete it, or move it above the exit if it was meant to run

`loadOne` answers later and nothing takes the answer. nothing waits for it and nothing observes its failure, so a failure surfaces elsewhere with no link to what started it Fix: await it, or state in the code what handles its result

`expect(add(1, 1)).toBe(add(1, 1));` has the same expression on both sides it holds the code to whatever the code already does, so it keeps passing through every change, including a change that breaks the behaviour Fix: write the expected value as a literal, instead of the call that produces it

`RegExp` runs on every pass of the loop. the same pattern is parsed and compiled on every pass when once would do, and compiling is the expensive half of matching Fix: compile it once above the loop and reuse it
Declared with `skip`. a skipped test reports success while the behaviour it names goes unchecked Fix: fix the test and enable it, or delete it and record what it was checking

Parameter `total` is reassigned inside the function. the caller's value changes without the call site saying so, which is hard to find when it turns out to be wrong Fix: assign to a local instead of `total`, and return the result

Parameter `value` is reassigned inside the function. the caller's value changes without the call site saying so, which is hard to find when it turns out to be wrong Fix: assign to a local instead of `value`, and return the result

`rqx-ignore with no reason` turns off a check that covers this code. the waiver is refused and the finding still counts, because a waiver that needs no justification allows a rule to be switched off one line at a time Fix: say why the finding is acceptable here, or fix it

the handler is only `throw error;` it reads as a decision about the failure and makes none, and in languages that rebuild the stack trace on rethrow it loses the original Fix: delete the handler so the failure propagates, or add handling specific to this level

`warmTheCache` runs when the file is loaded. it runs before any caller has asked for anything, in whatever order the imports resolve, and nothing can prevent it Fix: put it behind a function the caller chooses to call

`CsvWriter` is built by the object that holds it. nothing can be substituted for them, so every test of the owner has to set up the real collaborator and everything behind it Fix: accept it as an argument, so a caller can decide what it is

`0.1` is compared for exact equality a binary float rarely equals the decimal a person wrote, so a branch that depends on it is decided by rounding and not by the value Fix: compare the difference against a tolerance chosen for the domain

`countRows` answers something the line throws away. the code receives the result and ignores it, and nothing records what happens when the call fails Fix: handle the result, or state in the code why nothing needs to be done
